name: EL2244 / EL2444
tagline: Elantec's 120 MHz, 325 V/µs video dual, ranked beside the AD827 by CN/KR swap guides for neutral, detailed sound.

lineage.note: Dual/quad of the EL2044 on Elantec's complementary bipolar process. Codes EL2244CN/CS, EL2444CN/CS.
Bought Elantec in 2002; reissued the datasheet as FN7059 (© 2002–2004) and added Pb-free Z codes.
Owns the Intersil portfolio; a Renesas-branded datasheet exists. Lifecycle status unconfirmed.

part_numbers.note: Elantec 8-pin PDIP / SO; early datasheets call it EL2244C. Likely obsolete.
Pb-free 8-pin SO, tube and 13-inch reel (FN7059.2). Likely obsolete.
Quad: 14-pin PDIP / SO (0.150 in); early name EL2444C. Likely obsolete.
Pb-free 14-pin SO; reel variants in FN7059.2. Likely obsolete.

key_specs.value: 2.5 V to 36 V single (about ±1.25 V to ±18 V)

reputation.summary: Chinese sound-card and car head-unit modding (摩机) guides (Baidu Tieba's 40-op-amp list, PCPOP, 360doc, book118) rank it with the AD827 among the best voltage-feedback duals: neutral, a soundstage slightly wider than OP275, strong treble and resolution. They fault its thin mids, light bass and bland musicality, and call it hard to use well. Korea's digipine also lists it.
typical_uses: Op-amp swaps in PC sound cards
DIY I/V and buffer stages (CN/KR builds)
caveats: 120 MHz, 325 V/µs video part: needs tight decoupling and layout; may oscillate in sockets.
15 nV/√Hz input noise is high next to dedicated audio op-amps.
Praise is subjective and comes only from CN/KR modding sources.
Probably obsolete; supply is mainly old or broker stock.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit reports found. Old and probably obsolete, it reaches CN mod buyers via brokers, so treat DIP and SO stock of unverified provenance, Elantec-marked included, as possibly remarked. Pb-free 'Z' parts are a new number, not a die change.

refuted_claims: 'Roughly a 60 MHz class part': the FN7059 title and text give 120 MHz GBW; no 60 MHz figure found.
corrections: Process corrected to Elantec complementary bipolar, dual/quad of the EL2044 (120 MHz, 325 V/µs, 5.2 mA/amp).
